subject: Post-demo: Finova inference economics + validation tests
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@finova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Finova inference economics + validation tests

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on validation and commercial fit: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Live demo of Redwood hosted endpoint + Dedicated option and private deployment tradeoffs
- Baseline unit economics we sketched: ~ $85 / 1M tokens (hosted w/ 8k seq avg, no caching) vs hyperscaler claim of $120 / 1M tokens for comparable throughput
- Impact levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantized model option (FP16 -> 8-bit quant)

Proposed validation tests (short, prioritized)
1) Controlled 100k-token run: measure p50/p95 latency and realized cost per 1M tokens with your sample prompts (we'll run on both Hosted & Dedicated). Owner: Redwood (Ben) — target by Wed 5/19.
2) Cache-hit sensitivity: run with 0%, 30%, 60% prefix cache assumptions to show cost curve. Owner: Redwood (Karthik).
3) Batch-sizing sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16 to quantify latency vs throughput tradeoffs. Owner: Finova (you) + Redwood support.
4) Quality parity check vs Finova reference outputs for 200 prompts — to ensure quantization/variants don’t regress. Owner: Finova.

Attachments I sent: demo recording, proposed econ model, and a short one-page Redwood vs cloud-runner matrix (see attached).

Questions for Finova to confirm next week:
- Which 200 prompts should we use for the quality parity check? (Prefer a shared Drive folder)
- Any constraints on using a Dedicated pool vs hosted for the controlled runs? (billing/procurement preference)

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the first controlled run and share the measurement scripts + cost calc template.

Thanks —
Ava

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FW: Post-demo: Finova inference economics + validation tests

Quick technical notes and the cache emulation plan:

Cache definitions
- Prefix cache: store KV state for the first N tokens of a user prompt sequence; hits when subsequent requests share the same prefix. TTL: 10m for these tests.
- Session cache: per-session KV that persists for the session lifetime (simulate 30m).

Emulation script
- I will provide a small Python harness that replays the 200 prompts with configurable hit rate (0/30/60%). The harness will call the same endpoint and inject cached responses for hit cases to reflect reduced token generation.

Batching guidance (initial):
- Small (1): baseline latency; Good for interactive UX.
- Medium (4,8): sweet spot for p95 economics without huge latency hit.
- Large (16): best for throughput but expect p95 tail growth; use only for non-interactive pipelines.

I'll upload the harness and a short README to the Drive folder now; Ben, I left a note about the run window in the shared calendar.

Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
